rules: An original custodian can attest possession and liturgical veneration, not necessarily the historical biological identity of a medieval body.
Two monasteries may both report remains of a saint; a modern publication must not pronounce exclusive entire-body identity without independent provenance and source reconciliation.
A holy tomb, fragment, head reliquary, claimed translation and current reliquary are distinct evidence units.
A monastery's reported ecclesiastical recognition of an object is described within its historic context, not upgraded to modern independent authentication.
Competing claims are cross-linked by subject; one site-level map marker per canonical Place; no new pin for a fragment already grouped under its custodial Place.

dossiers.title_en: Saint Benedict of Nursia — attributed remains at Fleury and Montecassino
dossiers.title_fr: Saint Benoît de Nursie — dépouilles attribuées à Fleury et au Mont-Cassin

claimants.name: Abbaye de Fleury, Saint-Benoît-sur-Loire
claimants.claim: Monks report transfer from Montecassino around the late seventh century and relics now in their crypt, including annual procession.

claimants.name: Abbazia di Montecassino
claimants.claim: Abbey describes a joint tomb behind the main altar and silver containers holding attributed remains of Benedict and Scholastica; a postwar examination is narrated.

dossiers.finding_en: Both present Benedictine custodians document distinct bodily-relic traditions. Fleury reports translation from Montecassino; Montecassino maintains a combined burial of Benedict and Scholastica. Their reports are mutually important but do not settle what portion, if any, remains at each site. Neither claim is presented as independently authenticated.
dossiers.finding_fr: Les deux communautés bénédictines présentent des traditions de reliques corporelles distinctes : translation à Fleury, tombeau commun de Benoît et Scholastique au Mont-Cassin. Leurs sources ne permettent pas de déterminer indépendamment la part de dépouille qui se trouverait à chaque lieu ni d’en authentifier l’identité.
dossiers.open_question: Original inventories and historical translation sources, including exact extent of any material exchanged or left at Montecassino, require critical edition-level comparison.

dossiers.title_en: Saint Mary Magdalene — Provence and Vézelay relic traditions
dossiers.title_fr: Sainte Marie-Madeleine — traditions de reliques en Provence et à Vézelay

claimants.name: Basilique Sainte-Marie-Madeleine, Saint-Maximin
claimants.claim: Parish and diocese identify the crypt skull reliquary and narrate a 1279 discovery, later restoration, and processions; the head is a separately alleged bodily part.

claimants.name: Basilique Sainte-Marie-Madeleine, Vézelay
claimants.claim: The basilica identifies traditional Magdalene relics in its crypt and preserves the historic pilgrimage narrative, including medieval diffusion and disputed transfers.

dossiers.finding_en: Both Saint-Maximin and Vézelay document historical and continuing Magdalene devotions. Saint-Maximin's reported skull and Vézelay's reported crypt relics are not automatically the same object or mutually exclusive whole-body claims. Historical papal or monastic approval of a cult does not by itself establish modern material identification.
dossiers.finding_fr: Saint-Maximin et Vézelay attestent deux foyers du culte de Marie-Madeleine. Le crâne attribué de Saint-Maximin et les reliques de la crypte de Vézelay ne doivent être ni confondus ni artificiellement fusionnés. La reconnaissance historique d’un culte ne suffit pas à identifier matériellement les ossements.
dossiers.open_question: Trace the pre-1279 Vézelay inventory, the 1279 Saint-Maximin dossier and later distributions without treating mutually exclusive medieval hagiography as verified chain of custody.
